event.title: New York Mayor Calls for Federal Action Against Netanyahu Amid Arrest Warrant
event.canonical_title: New York Mayor Calls for Federal Action Against Netanyahu Amid Arrest Warrant
event.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that he lacks the authority to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, despite calling him a 'war criminal' and urging the US federal government to act on an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant issued in 2024. Mamdani emphasized that if Netanyahu visits the U.S., federal authorities should execute the warrant, as the city itself cannot enforce it.

timeline.title: New York Mayor Declares City Lacks Authority to Arrest Netanyahu on ICC Warrant
timeline.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated that the city does not have the authority to execute an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. He urged federal officials to take action regarding the warrant. Netanyahu's office has dismissed the warrant as illegitimate.

event_overview.title: About Netanyahu Arrest Warrant
event_overview.subject: Netanyahu Arrest Warrant
event_overview.summary: The Netanyahu arrest-warrant event concerns an International Criminal Court (ICC) warrant issued for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the Court’s Situation in the State of Palestine. The warrant has become a focus of debate over the ICC’s jurisdiction, the alleged crimes identified by the Court, and whether national or local authorities can or must act if Netanyahu travels abroad.

facts.label: Warrant date and court
facts.value: ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued an arrest warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu on November 21, 2024, in the ICC’s Situation in the State of Palestine.

facts.label: Allegations at the warrant stage
facts.value: The Chamber found reasonable grounds to believe Netanyahu was responsible for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity, including starvation as a method of warfare, murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts. These are allegations supporting a warrant, not a conviction.

facts.label: Underlying investigation
facts.value: The ICC Prosecutor opened the Situation in Palestine investigation on March 3, 2021; it covers alleged Rome Statute crimes committed since June 13, 2014. The Court had held that its territorial jurisdiction for this situation extends to Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

facts.label: Jurisdiction dispute
facts.value: On November 21, 2024, the same ICC chamber rejected Israel’s then-pending jurisdiction and notification challenges, stating that Israel’s acceptance was not required for the Court to exercise territorial jurisdiction based on Palestine and that the jurisdiction challenge was premature at that stage.

facts.label: Enforcement framework
facts.value: The ICC does not itself carry out arrests; arrest powers rest with states. States Parties to the Rome Statute have obligations to cooperate with ICC arrest-and-surrender requests, while the United States is not a party to the Rome Statute.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows New York City political and legal statements in July 2026 about possible action on the ICC warrant; it does not attempt to chronicle the full ICC case, the Gaza war, or all international responses to the warrant.
